cover: Houthi Red Sea advances, Crimean bridge strikes, and high-tech corporate fallout shake global capitals
cover_scene: A split composition showing an armed patrol along an arid desert coast beside a smoky marine horizon, contrasting with glowing digital stock exchange screens.

slides.scene: Military patrol vehicles and armed soldiers move through arid desert hills overlooking a narrow maritime strait, under hazy sun.
slides.headline: Forces Pull Back from Bab al-Mandab Strait
slides.body: Saudi-backed pro-government forces in Yemen have withdrawn from positions overlooking the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait to protect Aden. The redeployment allows advancing Houthi fighters to assert control over the vital Red Sea maritime chokepoint, risking further global trade disruption.

slides.scene: A massive road and rail bridge crossing a dark sea under a night sky filled with flashing explosions and drone silhouettes.
slides.headline: Ukraine Strikes Crimea Bridge in Massive Assault
slides.body: Russia reported that Ukraine targeted the strategic Crimea bridge in the conflict's largest drone strike to date. The assault, involving over 2,000 drones per BBC, hit the critical Russian supply route as air raid alerts echoed across Ukrainian cities.

slides.scene: A heavy rocket lifts off from a coastal launchpad at Cape Canaveral, billowing massive white exhaust plumes against a morning sky.
slides.headline: Vulcan Rocket Failure Destroys 40 Amazon Satellites
slides.body: A Vulcan rocket suffered an in-flight failure shortly after liftoff from Cape Canaveral, destroying its entire payload of 40 Amazon Leo satellites. The high-profile accident deals a sharp setback to Amazon's satellite deployment timeline and commercial space rivalry.

slides.scene: A spacious diplomatic conference hall in Shenzhen with national flags of the United States, China, and Russia arranged behind an empty table.
slides.headline: Beijing Prepares Groundbreaking Trilateral Superpower Summit
slides.body: China announced an upcoming trilateral summit in Shenzhen uniting Xi Jinping, Donald Trump, and Vladimir Putin during the APEC meeting. Washington aims to pursue discussions on nuclear arms reduction, an agenda item Beijing has previously resisted.
